taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana (now Sedum oreganum): flowering stems slender, erect or ascending, often curved, 8 cm to 15 cm long.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: a perennial from a creeping rootstock.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: rootstock rather slender, creeping.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: rootstock rather slender, creeping.

traits.clonal.note: Spreading in mats of rosettes, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 171894013, 129877060, 385525629, 5214529, 60390373, 177058909, 129783027, 60410052): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: basal leaves; the photos show them in tight rosettes.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: basal leaves 1 cm to 2 cm long.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: basal leaves spatulate-cuneate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Entire leaf edges, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 171894013, 129877060, 385525629, 5214529, 60390373, 177058909, 129783027, 60410052): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: basal leaves green and glabrous.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: inflorescence a rather congested cyme.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cymes 2 cm to 4 cm across, from the photos; Abrams (1944 p. 343) calls them congested.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 6 to 20 flowers and buds in a cyme, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 171894013, 129877060, 385525629, 5214529, 60390373, 177058909, 129783027, 60410052): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Five petals to a flower, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 171894013, 129877060, 385525629, 5214529, 60390373, 177058909, 129783027, 60410052): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Lanceolate lobes spreading in a star from a short base, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 171894013, 129877060, 385525629, 5214529, 60390373, 177058909, 129783027, 60410052): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: corolla 10 mm to 12 mm long, the lobes united about one-fourth the way.

traits.petal_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: the lobes lanceolate, long-acuminate.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowers 1.5 cm to 2 cm across, the lobes spreading from a short tube, from the photos.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: corolla yellow usually tinged with rose; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 343, Gormania oregana: flowering July to August.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: reddish flowering stems; tight rosettes of fleshy, glossy green spoon-shaped leaves, reddening in sun; clusters of yellow star flowers.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Oregon stonecrop from Abrams's description and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.135 m tall at 3 years in the open, within the flora's range. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
